items.abstract: <jats:p>We report herein the results of sedimentological and palynological analyses of a continuous core drilled through a ~4-m-thick clayey deposit here interpreted as an argillified loess, which filled up a karstic depression near the top of Monte Cònero, a 572-m-high calcareous promontory protruding on the Adriatic Sea just south of the port city of Ancona (Marche region of central Italy). This Middle to Upper Pleistocene loess deposit represents a unique occurrence in this north-eastern Apennine region, likely because it was preserved in a circumscribed karstic depression near the top of a mountain, which later became a swamp or a pond collecting just meteoric water, and thus it was prevented from post-depositional fluvial or aeolian erosion, or the accretion of siliciclastic material transported over there by the runoff or alluvial flooding. The source of this presumed aeolian sediment was the fine sand and silt that was deflated from the dry floor of the Adriatic basin during glacial maxima (i.e., the Penultimate Glacial Maximum and the Last Glacial Maximum) when, in fact, the global sea level was some 120-140 m lower than present. Another uniqueness of this deposit in the Palaeolithic context of the Umbria-Marche Apennines is that in the early 1960’s, 16 well-preserved bifaces knapped in situ from a distinctive local chert, were found in primary position at about 3-m-depth in this deposit during two well-documented archaeological excavation campaigns. These artefacts were originally attributed to a generic Acheulean lithic industry. In fact, our integrated sedimentological and palyno-stratigraphical analysis of this deposit suggests that this particular area of Monte Cònero was frequented by Acheulean hunters during some stages of the MIS 6 glacial period (i.e., 190-130 ka), and subsequently by Mousterian hunters through the Late Pleistocene cold period from MIS 5d to MIS 4.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Early hominin juvenile fossils are key for elucidating the developmental basis of adult phenotypic variation and enhancing our understanding of phylogenetic relationships. Since the discovery of the Taung child a century ago, numerous findings have expanded our knowledge concerning craniodental ontogeny of Australopithecus africanus and A. afarensis, and more recently, Paranthropus robustus. However, less is known about the derived, robust species P. boisei from eastern African. In this study, we present a juvenile maxilla specimen of P. boisei recently recovered from the Shungura Formation (Ethiopia), offering insights into the craniodental development of eastern African robust hominins. To give an age at death, the dental developmental stage was studied and compared to those of P. ­robustus individuals. We then examined the expression of derived morphological features, comparing them to those observed in various published fossils, in order to explore the craniofacial ontogeny of the genus Paranthropus. Our results show that OMO 362-10001 age at death is estimated to have been around 3.8 to 5 years old. The OMO 362-10001 maxillary morphology indicates that some of the derived features shared by species of the genus Paranthropus are already evident by this stage of development while others are not. This present ontogenetic pattern differs in some way from that of P. robustus, suggesting ontogenetic variation within the clade Paranthropus.</jats:p>
items.summary: 《埃塞俄比亚舒古拉组一件幼年上颌骨对鲍氏傍人生长发育的新启示》：该研究描述了一件新发现的鲍氏傍人幼年上颌骨标本，通过牙齿发育阶段估算其死亡年龄约为3.8至5岁，并与粗壮傍人个体比较，探讨傍人属的颅面生长发育。研究发现傍人属共有的一些衍生特征在该发育阶段已出现，而另一些尚未出现，且其生长发育模式与粗壮傍人存在差异，提示傍人支系内部存在生长发育变异。
items.title: New insights into the ontogeny of Paranthropus boisei offered by a juvenile maxilla from the Shungura Formation (Ethiopia)

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    The Levantine hominin fossil and archaeological records have played a central role in long‐standing palaeoanthropological debates over origin models and possible interbreeding between Neanderthals (
                    <jats:italic>Homo neanderthalensis</jats:italic>
                    ) and
                    <jats:italic>Homo sapiens</jats:italic>
                    . Recent research has provided a strong framework for the morphological expectations of recent hybrid ancestry in primates, along with renewed suggestions that early Late Pleistocene hominins from the Levant show morphological evidence of hybridization. Here we address these developments by using established diagnostic features of
                    <jats:italic>H. sapiens</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>H. neanderthalensis</jats:italic>
                    to review possible fossil evidence of hybridization from the key Levantine sites of Qafzeh, Skhūl, and Tabūn. We conclude that, while individuals from these sites show a perplexing combination of characteristics that broadly overlap with expectations of hybridization, this explanation can only be established once other alternatives have been ruled out, or through the recovery of genetic material from these key fossils.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Submarine caves are cryptic, climatically sensitive habitats with long‐term ecological dynamics that are poorly understood. We present the first palaeoecological analysis of bryozoans from Daidokutsu Cave (Okinawa, Japan), based on a sediment core spanning approximately the last 7000 years. We quantify temporal changes in bryozoan diversity, taxonomic and functional composition, and community turnover, comparing these with published records for ostracods, foraminifera and bivalves, as well as independent environmental proxies, that are, δ
                    <jats:sup>18</jats:sup>
                    O as a proxy for East Asian Winter Monsoon intensity and red soil input as a proxy for hydrodynamic energy, reflecting the winnowing of finer particles from terrigenous sediments deposited on coastal zones. The Daidokutsu bryozoan assemblage is relatively diverse, apparently highly endemic and dominated by erect colony forms. Diversity peaks mid‐record, consistent with partial cave isolation, then declines, likely towards a more specialised cave fauna, while the composition shows recurrent episodes of rapid turnover. No robust relationships emerge between bryozoan diversity and assemblage composition and the targeted environmental proxies, and detrended bryozoan diversity does not track East Asian Winter Monsoon variability as clearly as in ostracods, suggesting that bryozoans may be less sensitive to regional monsoon forcing. As the first quantitative multi‐taxon study of submarine cave evolution including bryozoans, our results show that bryozoan assemblages provide an independent perspective on long‐term ecological change, underscoring the need for further studies to assess more fully their potential as palaeoenvironmental indicators in cryptic shallow‐marine ecosystems.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Midventral skin glands secrete odors that mediate social contexts and are commonly found in rodents in the Cricetidae family rather than those in the Muridae family. African spiny mice (
                    <jats:italic>Acomys cahirinus</jats:italic>
                    ) are rodents in the family Muridae known for their remarkable regenerative abilities, menstruation, tail osteoderms, and unique social behaviors, including cooperative breeding, communal parenting, and low aggression. They are also related to gerbils (
                    <jats:italic>Meriones</jats:italic>
                    ), which are among the few murids that lack preputial glands and instead scent‐mark with midventral glands.
                    <jats:italic>Acomys</jats:italic>
                    also lack preputial glands, but whether they have midventral glands is less well known. Here, we determined that
                    <jats:italic>Acomys</jats:italic>
                    have midventral glands near the umbilicus. As in
                    <jats:italic>Meriones</jats:italic>
                    , male
                    <jats:italic>Acomys</jats:italic>
                    had larger midventral glands that were visible after depilation. Immunohistochemistry showed that midventral glands in both sexes were positive for androgen receptors, suggesting they may be under androgen control. This investigation provides basic information on the presence, location, structure, and sexual dimorphism of the midventral glands in
                    <jats:italic>Acomys</jats:italic>
                    , providing a morphological baseline for comparative studies of social signaling across the Muridae family.
                  </jats:p>
authors: Jacqueline Cupo, Malcolm Maden, Justin Varholick
